parties: DOMS Industries Limited (acquirer) vs. Newell Brands Inc. and subsidiaries (Reynolds Pens India and five other entities) (seller)
headline: DOMS acquires Reynolds brand worldwide rights from Newell Brands for $3.7M
sum: DOMS Industries, a Gujarat-based stationery manufacturer, acquired worldwide rights to the Reynolds brand and related assets from Newell Brands subsidiaries for $3.7 million. The transaction includes identified contracts, employees, liabilities and IP across six Newell entities operating in multiple jurisdictions, expanding DOMS' writing instruments portfolio.
implication: Cross-border acquisition of iconic consumer brand with multi-jurisdictional IP, employment and tax considerations sets precedent for Indian mid-market players acquiring mature Western brand portfolios via asset purchase structure; employment novation and indirect tax compliance (GST on IP transfer, forex regulations) are the critical gating items.
detail: DOMS Industries Limited, founded in 2006 and headquartered in Valsad, Gujarat, acquired the Reynolds brand (a heritage writing instrument brand) and specified assets, employees, contracts and liabilities from Reynolds Pens India and five other Newell Brands Inc. subsidiaries. The deal required comprehensive IP due diligence across multiple jurisdictions, employment novation to DOMS, contract transfers (including distributor and supply agreements), and multi-jurisdictional direct and indirect tax compliance (including GST treatment of IP transfer, withholding tax on cross-border payments, and forex regulations). The transaction strengthens DOMS' competitive position in India's fast-moving consumer stationery segment and expands its international footprint via the Reynolds brand.

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961, Sections 194LA, 195 (withholding on cross-border IP/asset payments)
framework.note: central - governs tax deduction and remittance on $3.7M cross-border payment to Newell Brands entities

framework.ref: Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, Chapter V (IP transfer, supply of services)
framework.note: central - GST classification and rate applicable to transfer of intellectual property (Reynolds brand, trademarks) and identified assets

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999, Sections 4, 6 (current account remittance, FEMA approval)
framework.note: central - governs approval for outbound remittance of $3.7M for acquisition; RBI Liberalised Remittance Scheme or Schedule I approval may apply

framework.ref: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Sections 47–54 (sale of goods and intangible assets)
framework.note: amended - governs contractual rights, assignment and novation of distributor and supply contracts; review for assumption of liabilities

framework.ref: The Trade Marks Act, 1999, Sections 37–47 (assignment and transmission of registered trademarks)
framework.note: central - governs registration of Reynolds trademark transfer to DOMS; may require filing with Intellectual Property Office of India (IPOI)

framework.ref: Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, Sections 25–26 (employee transfer, novation of contracts)
framework.note: central - governs absorption of employees from Newell entities into DOMS; payment of gratuity, notice and severance protections

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013, Sections 184–186 (acquisitions, related party transactions if applicable)
framework.note: amended - DOMS board approval, disclosure in annual reports; material acquisitions may trigger CSR obligations under Schedule VII

framework.ref: Competition Act, 2002, Sections 5–6 (merger control, CCI pre-clearance)
framework.note: amended - assess if transaction triggers CCI notification thresholds (asset value, turnover); likely sub-threshold given $3.7M value but must verify Newell Brands' Indian turnover

framework.ref: Transfer of Property Act, 1882, Sections 5–6 (transfer of identified assets, immovable and movable)
framework.note: central - governs mechanics of asset transfer; ensure clear identification and schedule of transferred contracts, IP, inventory, receivables

structure.consideration: $3.7 million (all-cash cross-border payment to Newell Brands entities)
conditions: IP due diligence clearance (Reynolds trademarks, copyrights, design registrations worldwide)
Employee novation agreements with absorbed workforce (Reynolds Pens India staff and transferred employees)
Consent of counterparties to material contracts (distributor agreements, supply contracts, licensing arrangements)
Third-party clearance / waiver of change-of-control provisions in identified contracts
Tax clearance certificate from Newell Brands entities confirming no outstanding Indian tax liabilities
approvals: RBI / FEMA approval for outbound remittance of $3.7M under appropriate Schedule or Liberalised Remittance Scheme
IPOI registration of Reynolds trademark assignment and transmission
DOMS Industries board resolution (likely related party if any Newell director overlap; verify independence)
CCI pre-merger notification (if transaction value or turnover thresholds triggered; likely clearance given asset value)
Foreign Company (FDI) compliance if Newell Brands deemed foreign investor retaining residual liabilities
structure.novel: Cross-border acquisition by Indian mid-market consumer goods player of a heritage international brand; employment novation across multiple jurisdictions; worldwide IP transfer (Reynolds brand rights in multiple countries) via single transaction structure.

triggers.note: Cross-border payment of $3.7M triggers RBI approval requirement; must confirm Schedule I general permission or specific FEMA approval route

Withholding tax (2% on payments for management/technical expertise or IP; 10–30% on other cross-border payments) on $3.7M remittance to Newell entities; treaty benefit analysis (US–India Tax Treaty) may reduce rate
GST classification of Reynolds brand and asset transfer (IP treated as supply of service; typically 5% or 18% depending on classification); reverse charge mechanism if Newell deemed foreign supplier
Registration of trademark assignment with IPOI; worldwide Reynolds trademarks may require separate filings in jurisdictions where DOMS operates
Employee absorption from Reynolds Pens India and other entities; calculation of gratuity, leave encashment, and other statutory termination benefits for transferred staff
